title: HPRO: Hierarchical Progressive Reward Optimization via Preference Extraction for Emotional Text-to-Speech
abstract: Recently, Large Language Model (LLM)-based Text-to-Speech (TTS) models have achieved remarkable naturalness. However, the standard Supervised Fine-Tuning paradigm often converges to statistically averaged prosody, limiting emotional expressiveness. While preference-driven optimization offers a promising alternative, existing approaches suffer from two structural mismatches: information conflict, where content and emotion in a shared latent space produce conflicting gradients, leading to reward hacking and semantic degradation; and scale gap, where sparse sentence-level rewards struggle to guide dense frame-level generation. To overcome these challenges, we propose HPRO, a hierarchical progressive reward optimization framework. Within HPRO, we introduce the HD-Emo codec as a novel differentiable reward model to resolve the information conflict. It extracts speech into distinct content and style preference tokens, structurally isolating emotional optimization from semantic content. Building upon this structured preference space, HPRO bridges the scale gap by progressively aligning frame-, word- and sentence-level objectives. Experiments demonstrate that HPRO significantly enhances emotional expressiveness, while effectively preserving linguistic intelligibility. The code and audio samples are publicly available at https://xxh333.github.io/hpro-demo/.

significance.justification: The paper refines the preference-driven optimization technique for TTS by addressing structural mismatches, offering measurable gains in emotional expressiveness while preserving intelligibility, which directly impacts how builders might approach fine-tuning LLM-based TTS systems.

novelty.justification: The paper introduces the novel HD-Emo codec to structurally isolate content and style tokens and proposes a hierarchical progressive alignment framework, representing a substantial new variation distinct from prior preference optimization approaches in TTS.

reproducibility.justification: The paper states that code and audio samples are publicly available at a provided URL, indicating that code and most artifacts are public, with only minor potential friction for full reproduction.

clarity.justification: The paper is solidly written, clearly defining the problems of information conflict and scale gap, and presents a defensible evaluation methodology comparing HPRO against baselines on emotional expressiveness and intelligibility.

topical_fit.justification: The paper is clearly in scope as it focuses on optimizing LLM-based Text-to-Speech models, though its specific application to emotional TTS makes it relevant to builders rather than the central focus of all LLM applications.
